title: 1996 AMC 8 Problem 24
statement: The measure of angle \(ABC\) is \(50^\circ.\) \(\overline{AD}\) bisects angle \(BAC,\) and \(\overline{DC}\) bisects angle \(BCA.\) The measure of angle \(ADC\) is

solutions.text:
In triangle \(ABC,\) \[ \begin{aligned} \angle BAC + \angle BCA &= 180^\circ - 50^\circ \\ &= 130^\circ. \end{aligned} \]

The bisectors give \(\angle DAC + \angle DCA = \tfrac{130^\circ}{2} = 65^\circ.\) In triangle \(ADC,\) \(\angle ADC = 180^\circ - 65^\circ = 115^\circ.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C .
hints: In triangle \(ABC,\) angles \(BAC\) and \(BCA\) add to \(180^\circ - 50^\circ = 130^\circ\)
The bisected halves at \(A\) and \(C\) add to \(65^\circ;\) use the angle sum in triangle \(ADC\)
